note: An attachment compressed with a method that is neither stored nor deflate. Section 7's remedy is proportionate rather than uniform: if the ROOT DOCUMENT used such a method the archive is refused, because there is no document to return, but if an attachment did, the reader drops that attachment, records a diagnostic and returns the document. Refusing a whole library because one photograph used an unusual method would be disproportionate. Nothing in the corpus reached that remedy before this file. THE DROPPED ENTRY'S NAME CARRIES BOTH CHARACTERS RFC 6901 ESCAPES, and that is load-bearing rather than realistic. Section 6.3 puts a container diagnostic in the `#/entries/` pointer space, because an archive entry is not part of the document and no pointer into the document can locate one - and there the member name is ONE reference token: a `/` inside it MUST be written `~1` and a `~` MUST be written `~0`, with `~` escaped first. `photos/a~b.jpg` exercises both, and their ORDER as well - escaping `/` first and `~` second turns `~1` into `~01`, so a reader that reverses the two produces a different path from one that does not. An attachment name is the one place in this format where a member name routinely contains a slash, A reader that forgets to escape emits `#/entries/photos/a~b.jpg`, which no runner will match, while every attachment name free of those two characters passes whether a reader escapes at all. Renaming this entry to something flat removes the coverage and nothing goes red. `notes/readable.txt` is kept and listed, so the drop is provably scoped rather than total: a reader that dropped every attachment on meeting one bad method would otherwise pass. The body of the dropped entry is not valid bzip2 data and never could be read as any, deliberately - a conforming reader refuses it on the METHOD, before attempting to decompress. A reader that inflated first would fail on the body and could report the wrong cause, and this file cannot tell those two apart, which is a limitation rather than a defect. Method 12 is legal in APPNOTE and simply not available in every target language, which is what section 7 is about; the case would work the same with any method outside stored and deflate. This archive is hand-built, because archive/zip refuses to write a method it has no compressor for - which is every method but the two section 7 allows.
